title: The Devil Is in the Interface: Evaluating How Tool Architecture Shapes Coding Agent Behavior
abstract: arXiv:2608.11386v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As large language models continue to improve, agentic systems are becoming increasingly important, and tools are a key design dimension because they determine how agents access information and take action in their environments. Prior work on agent tooling has primarily focused on expanding what agents can do, but has paid less systematic attention to how those capabilities are organized and exposed to the model. We refer to this latter design dimension as tool architecture. We study tool architecture in coding agents through controlled experiments on repository-level issue fixing, comparing six tool architectures that hold the underlying information and actions similar while varying how they are organized and exposed to the model, across three actors and a total of 11,700 trajectories. translated_title: 魔鬼在于界面：评估工具架构如何塑造编码代理行为
translated_abstract: 摘要：随着大型语言模型的持续改进，代理系统变得越来越重要，而工具是一个关键的设计维度，因为它们决定了代理如何访问信息并在环境中采取行动。先前关于代理工具的研究主要侧重于扩展代理能做什么，但较少系统性地关注这些能力如何组织和暴露给模型。我们将后一个设计维度称为工具架构。我们通过在仓库级问题修复上的受控实验来研究编码代理中的工具架构，比较了六种工具架构，这些架构在保持底层信息和操作相似的同时，改变了它们如何组织和暴露给模型，涉及三个执行者，共计11,700条轨迹。我们的实验表明，即使工具提供类似的能力，工具架构也会改变代理行为：与一个基础架构相比，其中……
tldr: 本文通过受控实验揭示，工具架构（即工具的组织和暴露方式）即使在不改变工具功能的情况下，也能显著影响编码代理的行为和问题解决效率。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals through controlled experiments that tool architecture—how tools are organized and exposed—significantly influences coding agent behavior and problem-solving efficiency, even when tool capabilities remain unchanged.
